title: India's Young Seamers Surge as ICC Women's Rankings Reward Raipur Form
excerpt: Nandani Sharma leaps 26 places and Kranti Gaud nine, with Sree Charani and Deepti Sharma still ranked first and second, while Australia's veterans gain in the ODI lists.
body:
• India's Nandani Sharma has jumped 26 places to 45th in the ICC Women's T20I bowling rankings, with Kranti Gaud up nine places to 43rd, after India took a 2-0 lead over Zimbabwe in Raipur.
  • Sree Charani and Deepti Sharma still hold first and second place in the T20I bowling list, giving India four bowlers moving the right way in one update.
  • Shafali Verma stays fourth among T20I batters after 55 off 25 balls in the second match.
  • In the ODI lists, Australia's Megan Schutt rose to fourth among bowlers and Ellyse Perry to ninth among batters after a 3-0 sweep of Bangladesh.

India's young seamers have been rewarded for a series that is not even finished. With India 2-0 up against Zimbabwe in Raipur, Nandani Sharma and Kranti Gaud made the largest moves in the latest ICC Women's T20I bowling rankings, while the top of the list stayed Indian.

Nandani is the joint leading wicket-taker across the first two matches with three wickets, including two for 11 in the opener, and gains 26 places to 45th with a career-best 507 rating points, according to the ICC. Gaud, who took one for 16 in the first match and one for 15 in the second, climbs nine places to 43rd.

India Hold the Top, Too

The climbers are chasing their own teammates. Sree Charani remains first and Deepti Sharma second in the T20I bowling rankings after economical returns against Zimbabwe, which means India's depth, not just its stars, is what the table now shows.

With the bat, Shafali Verma remains fourth in the T20I batting rankings after striking 55 from 25 balls in the second match, and Deepti moved up one place to joint 37th after her 49 off 37 in the opener, MyKhel reported. Zimbabwe's Kelis Ndhlovu rose to 64th, Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano to 73rd and Josephine Nkomo to 91st, with Sharne Meyers returning to the top 100 at 96th after an unbeaten 43.

The Trans-Tasman Movement

The first Australia-New Zealand T20I in Sydney, won narrowly by Australia, moved a different set of names. Annabel Sutherland rose one place to eighth among T20I bowlers, Jess Kerr climbed five spots to 17th, and Bree Illing and Nensi Patel reached career-best positions of 23rd and 35th.

Among batters, New Zealand's Georgia Plimmer jumped 13 places to 48th after a career-best unbeaten 85 in a 127-run stand, and Maddy Green rose three places to 34th with a career-best 528 points. Australia's Beth Mooney remains the world's No. 1 T20I batter.

Australia's Veterans Gain in ODIs

The ODI charts reflected Australia's completed 3-0 series sweep of Bangladesh in the ICC Women's Championship. Veteran seamer Megan Schutt climbed to fourth among ODI bowlers. Ellyse Perry moved up to ninth among ODI batters and jumped 14 places to 25th among all-rounders, while Sutherland rose four places to 13th among batters after an unbeaten half-century in the final ODI. Bangladesh's Sharmin Akhter Supta climbed five places to 25th among ODI batters.

What's Next

India close out the Zimbabwe series with a 3-0 whitewash in reach, and another strong return from Nandani or Gaud would push both toward the top 40. The rankings are a snapshot; the pattern underneath them, of India producing ranked bowlers in batches, is the longer story.
